title: Closed subschemes are limits of their stage scheme-theoretic images
statement: Let $J$ be a small nonempty cofiltered category and $D:J\to\mathsf{Scheme}$ a diagram of schemes [def-pc-scheme]. Suppose every $D_j$ is quasi-compact [def-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-scheme] and quasi-separated (the intersection of any two quasi-compact open subsets is quasi-compact), and every transition morphism is affine [pqf-def-affine-morphism]. Let $\pi_Y$ be a limit cone with vertex $Y$ and let $i:X\to Y$ be a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion]. Then there exist a diagram $Z:J\to\mathsf{Scheme}$, a natural transformation $k:Z\to D$ with closed immersion components, and a cone $\pi_X$ with vertex $X$, such that $X$ is its limit, every transition of $Z$ is affine, and $\pi_{X,j}\mathbin{;}k_j=i\mathbin{;}\pi_{Y,j}$ for every $j\in J$ (composition written in diagram order).

proof.text: The limit projections are affine by isAffineHom_π_app. Hence i followed by a projection is quasi-compact. For each j take the scheme-theoretic image Z_j with its closed inclusion k_j and factorization of X → D_j. The kernel description on affine opens supplies these images.

For an arrow j → l, the composite Z_j → D_j → D_l factors through Z_l: functions in the image ideal at l map to zero on X and hence vanish in the image ring at j. The unique factorization defines Z_j → Z_l. Monicity of k_l proves composition, identities, naturality, and the cone equations. The induced map from Z_j into Z_l × over D_l with D_j is a closed immersion since its composite to D_j is k_j. The projection of this pullback to Z_l is affine, so transitions of Z are affine.

Fix an affine open of a stage and restrict to its over category. The affine inverse images have rings B_j with filtered colimit B; X over their limit is Spec(B/I). The image over each stage open is Spec(B_j/ker(B_j → B/I)). Every element of B/I comes from some B_j. If an element of an image ring maps to zero in B/I, it is already zero by the definition of that kernel. Thus these quotient rings have colimit B/I. Spec turns this into a limit, giving the limit property locally on every such affine open.

The local identifications and factorizations agree on overlaps by uniqueness of the maps into the closed images. They therefore glue. For a test cone, first use the limit property of Y to get its map to Y, and then use these affine local identifications to factor it uniquely through X. This is the IsLimit structure on the displayed cone.

lean.statement:
theorem exists_closed_image_limit_system
    {J : Type u} [SmallCategory J] [IsCofiltered J]
    (D : J ⥤ Scheme.{u})
    [∀ {j k : J} (a : j ⟶ k), IsAffineHom (D.map a)]
    [∀ j : J, CompactSpace (D.obj j)]
    [∀ j : J, QuasiSeparatedSpace (D.obj j)]
    {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (i : X ⟶ Y) [IsClosedImmersion i]
    (πY : (Functor.const J).obj Y ⟶ D) (hY : IsLimit (Cone.mk Y πY)) :
    ∃ (Z : J ⥤ Scheme.{u}) (k : Z ⟶ D)
      (πX : (Functor.const J).obj X ⟶ Z),
      Nonempty (IsLimit (Cone.mk X πX)) ∧
      (∀ {j k : J} (a : j ⟶ k), IsAffineHom (Z.map a)) ∧
      (∀ j : J, IsClosedImmersion (k.app j)) ∧
      (∀ j : J, πX.app j ≫ k.app j = i ≫ πY.app j)
